about: Domaine de la Chevalerie sits in Restigné, beside Bourgueil on the right bank of the Loire, and is one of the oldest family estates in the appellation. The Caslot family traces its vines here to 1640, when an ancestor, Pierre Caslot, began planting at the lieu-dit Chevalerie, and some thirteen generations have followed. A later Pierre Caslot built the estate’s modern reputation and its range of single-vineyard wines; since 2022 his children Laurie and Emmanuel have run the domaine.

The estate grows only Cabernet Franc, on about 33 hectares within a few kilometres of the cellar, farmed organically and biodynamically. This cuvée comes from the Chevalerie lieu-dit around the house itself, on clay with micaceous chalk over the region’s tuffeau limestone, from vines around sixty years old. Fermentation uses native yeasts in concrete and stainless vats with long, gentle macerations; the wines age in old oak and finish their rest in cellars dug into the tuffeau, naturally held at about 12°C.

Chevalerie is built to age, with the darker, firmer side of Bourgueil: red currant, raspberry and black cherry, with the graphite, dried herbs and earthy notes that Loire Cabernet Franc takes on from limestone. At six-plus years old, the 2019 is entering the window where that savoury complexity begins to show, and the estate suggests about a decade of potential for this cuvée.
